## Installation **Command** ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/spinner ``` **Manual** Use React 19, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS v4 with the shadcn semantic colour tokens. Follow the [manual setup guide](https://cadence.dev/docs/installation#manual-installation) for the base CSS and aliases; copying files does not require the shadcn CLI. 1. Install the component's complete recursive npm dependencies (versions are preserved). Example-only packages are listed separately below when needed. ```package-manager npm install clsx tailwind-merge motion lucide-react ``` 2. Copy the following registry dependencies in the listed dependency order. Each JSON link exposes every file's full `content` and `target`; copy all files, including multi-file helpers. - [@cadence/cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) — direct registry dependency. - [@cadence/cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) — direct registry dependency. 3. Place every file at its target below. `@components` means your components directory, for example `src/components`; keep the remaining `cadence/` tree and relative imports intact. Each source block on the website copies the entire file, including folded lines. | Item | Target file | Full source | | --- | --- | --- | | cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/motion.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) | | cadence-motion | `@components/cadence/lib/geometry.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) | | cadence-utils | `@components/cadence/lib/cn.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/provider.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/popup-style.ts` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/control-animation.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/native-div.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | cadence-provider | `@components/cadence/lib/press-button.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) | | spinner | `@components/cadence/spinner/index.tsx` | [JSON files[].content](https://cadence.dev/r/spinner.json) | [Source files: cadence-motion](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-motion.json) [Source files: cadence-utils](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-utils.json) [Source files: cadence-provider](https://cadence.dev/r/cadence-provider.json) [Source files: spinner](https://cadence.dev/r/spinner.json) 4. Apply the required CSS/configuration below, then follow [Usage](#usage) for the component imports and composition. No additional item-specific CSS configuration is required beyond the base theme. The provider files above are required imports. Wrapping your application is optional; standalone components respect the system motion preference. To control a subtree, wrap it once: ```tsx import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider"; export function MotionRoot({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { return {children}; } ``` Copy all nine files in the target list, keeping `spinner/index.tsx` beside the shared `lib/` directory and preserving relative imports and `"use client"` directives. The glyph uses a CSS loop, but its `useCadenceMotion` import still requires the provider files and their `motion` dependency. Copy every file from the motion, utilities and provider payloads; wrapping the application in `CadenceProvider` is optional. Without a wrapper, Spinner follows the system motion preference. Full and reduced both keep the single-glyph `animate-spin` rotation, the animation system's specific reduced-motion exception. None uses `animate-none` and leaves the named icon visible and still. Tailwind's `--animate-spin` theme token owns the loop clock; provider `timeScale`, including zero, does not change it. Use `mode="none"` on the included provider to stop the loop, as the explicit `data-motion="none"` example does from its first render. No additional item-specific CSS is required beyond the base theme and Tailwind utilities. Inside a button also uses [Button](/components/button). Install it when copying that example: ```install npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/button ``` For a manual Button installation, follow its Manual tab too; it adds `button/index.tsx`, `@base-ui/react` and `class-variance-authority` alongside the shared files and packages already listed here. Usage, Sized by the caller, A specific label, `data-motion="none"` and the top specimen need no other registry items, npm packages or assets. `lucide-react` is already an implementation dependency for the loading glyph; the site's preview shell is not consumer setup. In Next.js App Router, all five body examples can be composed in a Server Component with their shown serializable props, including the nested provider. Keep the installed sources' client boundaries. A caller that adds React state, event handlers or browser APIs needs its own client module. The examples are fixed loading states: the caller starts and finishes requests, mounts or removes Spinner, sets and clears the region's `aria-busy`, and exposes completion or error feedback. Keep a meaningful status label; inside the pending button, keep its written label, `disabled` and `aria-busy`, and hide the redundant glyph with `aria-hidden`. Reserve any changing label width and choose icon sizes that fit the surrounding layout. ## Usage ```tsx import { Spinner } from "@/components/cadence/spinner"; export function LoadingRegistry() { return (
Loading the registry…
); } ``` ## Inside a button Keep the button’s written label and disable it while work is pending. `aria-busy` names the button’s busy state; hide the redundant spinner glyph from assistive technology here so it does not duplicate that label. This fixed pending state does not start a request or own its lifetime. If switching from an idle label changes the width, reserve that width in the caller’s layout. ```tsx import { Button } from "@/components/cadence/button"; import { Spinner } from "@/components/cadence/spinner"; export function SavingButton() { return ( ); } ``` ## Sized by the caller The icon is `size-4` by default and inherits `currentColor`. The fixed 12, 16, 24 and 32 pixel specimens show caller classes rather than a finite `size` prop. Muted text colour belongs to the first specimen only; each glyph keeps its own accessible loading status and inherits header motion. ```tsx import { Spinner } from "@/components/cadence/spinner"; export function SpinnerSizes() { return (
); } ``` ## A specific label “Loading” is the default accessible name. Say what is loading when surrounding text does not: this standalone status announces “Saving invoice” without adding a focus stop. The caller decides when to mount it and must expose completion or an error through its own result UI. ```tsx import { Spinner } from "@/components/cadence/spinner"; export function SavingInvoice() { return ; } ``` ## Under `data-motion="none"` This example explicitly fixes its provider to `none` from the first render, independently of the header. The spinner stays visible and named, with no rotation or running animation; it is not a post-mount mode switch. Other examples inherit the header. Both full and reduced keep Spinner’s single-glyph rotation, the animation system’s specific reduced-motion exception. ```tsx import { CadenceProvider } from "@/components/cadence/lib/provider"; import { Spinner } from "@/components/cadence/spinner"; export function StaticSpinner() { return ( Loading the registry… ); } ``` ## When to use - An action the user just triggered: save, send, invite, publish. The spinner sits where the user is looking — inside the button, or immediately beside it. - A wait with no measurable progress: a request that returns when it returns. - A region that is loading and whose shape you cannot predict. When you *can* predict it, use `skeleton` instead: it keeps the layout stable. ## When not to use - A wait under about 300 ms. The spinner appears and disappears before it can be read, which reads as a flicker. Keep the button's label and disable it. - A known percentage. Use `progress`; a spinning wheel after "60%" is a regression. - A page that is loading its first paint. There is nothing to spin inside yet — a skeleton or a server-rendered shell is better. - A decorative "we're working on it" on a marketing page. Motion without a state change is decoration (P9). ## API | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ----------- | -------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | | `className` | `string` | – | Merged last — size and colour live here (`size-3`, `text-…`). | | `aria-label`| `string` | `"Loading"` | The accessible name; pass a specific one when it helps. | All native `svg` props are forwarded. `data-slot="spinner"` and `data-motion` are always set, and `role="status"` with the label is the announcement. ## Motion contract Recipe: `data.transition`, continuous form. The loop is CSS (`animate-spin`) rather than Motion, for the same reason as `skeleton`: a spinner is by definition next to work the user is waiting on, and it must not add a frame callback to it. Only `transform` (rotation) changes, so the loop can never trigger layout. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------- | | spin | `rotate 0 → 360deg` | `data.transition` / `animate-spin` (theme timing) | yes (CSS) | | reduced | same rotation | `animate-spin` | yes (CSS) | | none | none; icon static | `animate-none` | – | Reduced keeps the rotation on purpose: M5 removes travel and scale, and a rotation in place is neither. A spinner that freezes under reduced motion would read as a frozen app. `none` stops it completely, which is what a screenshot test or a print stylesheet needs. ## Keyboard interactions None. The spinner is not focusable and takes no input; focus stays on the control that started the work, which is where the user's next action will be. ## Accessibility - `role="status"` is a polite live region: the label is announced when the spinner appears, without interrupting. Do not wrap it in another `aria-live` region. - The label must carry the meaning. The rotation is never the only signal, and under `data-motion="none"` it is not a signal at all. - Give the busy region `aria-busy="true"` and remove it when the work finishes, so the state survives even if the spinner unmounts early. - Do not replace a button's label with a spinner and nothing else. Keep the word, or add an `sr-only` copy, or the control loses its name mid-action. - Do not stack spinners. One per action; a page with five is a page with no feedback. ## Responsive behavior The spinner is an inline icon, so it follows the text it sits in. Inside a button it keeps the button's height; inside a heading, size it down (`size-3`) or it will dominate the line. On touch targets, keep the surrounding button at least 44×44 by size, not by growing the icon. ## Performance - One CSS animation per element, on `transform` only; no JS loop, no layout read. - Compositor-friendly, but the animation-system budget still applies: fewer than twenty simultaneously animating elements. For a list of pending rows, render one spinner for the list, not one per row. - No `will-change`: the browser promotes a transform animation on its own. ## Notes for AI - Use `spinner` for an action, `skeleton` for a layout. Getting this backwards is the most common loading-state mistake: a skeleton in a button, or a spinner where the content shape was known all along. - Keep the button's text; add the spinner in front of it and disable the button. - Under `data-motion="none"` the icon stays visible. Do not hide it to "respect" the preference — the state still has to be visible.
